recap: Troy Bolcerek's shot with 5.2 seconds left won it. G-E-T led 49–47 going into the fourth quarter.
Bolcerek scored 14 of his 19 points in the first half, and Bangor led 29–24 at halftime. Chris Chandler had 17 points and 17 rebounds.
Kyle Schroeder had three steals for breakaway layups in the third quarter, as Bangor went on a 13–4 run to put the game away.

The game was tied 14–14 at halftime, and Bangor led 21–17 after three quarters. Fourth-quarter 3-pointers from Kyle Schroeder and Brandon Meyer held off Royall, and Bangor went into the Christmas break 5–0.

The game was tied 32–32 at halftime, but Bangor outscored Hillsboro 24–7 in the third quarter to stay perfect at 9–0. Troy Bolcerek scored 17 of his 24 points in the second half. Hillsboro's Greg Jefferies led all scorers with 26.

Bangor opened with a 16–0 run and led 19–2 after one quarter, hitting four of its 10 3-pointers in the first. West Salem cut it to 48–35 after three, but Bangor won the fourth 22–14 and went 20 of 23 from the free-throw line to reach 10–0.

Lukas Ermis, Kyle Schroeder, Brandon Meyer and Eddie Ikert hit consecutive 3-pointers for a 26–13 lead early in the second quarter, and Cashton got no closer than 13 after Bangor went up 35–17. Troy Bolcerek, playing on an ankle he injured three days earlier, had 22 points, 9 rebounds and 2 blocked shots in front of 750 fans as Bangor went to 11–0.

Auburndale coach Tim Anderson, a 1963 Bangor graduate, was honored before the game and won his 501st career game in front of a capacity crowd. Bangor led 11–9 after one quarter, but Auburndale (13–0, No. 2 in Division 3) scored the next eight points and pulled away. Troy Bolcerek re-sprained his ankle midway through the second quarter, and Bangor shot 9 for 40 in its first loss.
Troy Bolcerek, hampered by a sprained left ankle, helped Bangor, ranked ninth in Division 4, stay unbeaten in the Scenic Bluffs at 8–0. Danny Sullivan led Wonewoc-Center with 26 points.
Trailing by a point with less than a minute to play, Kyle Schroeder made a steal and a layup, and Bangor escaped to stay unbeaten in the Scenic Bluffs at 9–0.

Troy Bolcerek's 3-pointer at the buzzer won it in overtime. Royall's Sam Overlien hit a fadeaway jumper for a 45–43 lead, the officials put the clock back to three seconds, and Kyle Schroeder's baseball pass found Bolcerek just behind the arc. Royall had tied it 41–41 on an Overlien 3 with 1:45 left in regulation, and Bolcerek scored five of his 19 points in overtime as Bangor went to 10–0 in the Scenic Bluffs.

Troy Bolcerek scored his 1,000th career point in the fourth quarter and led all scorers with 24 points and seven rebounds, as Bangor clinched at least a share of the Scenic Bluffs title. Bangor opened on a 14–2 run, led 37–27 at halftime and by 15 after three quarters.
Troy Bolcerek scored nine points in the second quarter to break open a 15–15 game, and Bangor, ranked seventh in Division 4, led by eight at halftime. Bolcerek had nine rebounds.

Bangor trailed by three at halftime, then Chris Chandler scored six points in the third quarter to break the game open. Hillsboro rallied with four 3-pointers in the fourth, three by Drew Alexander, but Scenic Bluffs champion Bangor held on to go 13–0 in the league. Hillsboro made nine 3-pointers, five by Greg Jefferies. (The paper's quarter scores for Hillsboro add to 54, one more than its final, so its third and fourth quarters are left blank.)

Bangor led 19–17 after one quarter and outscored Cashton 24–15 in the second for a 43–32 halftime lead. Troy Bolcerek scored 27 points with four 3-pointers, and Bangor finished 14–0 in the Scenic Bluffs, the first team to go unbeaten in the conference since Wonewoc-Center in 1992–93.
Bangor, ranked fifth in Division 4 by the Associated Press, led 41–9 at halftime of the WIAA Division 4 regional first round.

Troy Bolcerek scored nine of his 21 points in the first quarter and added six assists and five rebounds, and the top-seeded Cardinals led 31–20 at halftime of the regional semifinal for their 10th straight win.

event: WIAA Division 4 regional final at Wonewoc-Center
recap: Bangor never trailed but struggled from the field and went 4 for 13 from the free-throw line. With 3:29 left, Brandon Meyer made a steal and deflected it to Kyle Schroeder, who scored and was fouled for a 50–45 lead, and Brookwood scored just two more points. Troy Bolcerek scored nine of his 24 points in the fourth quarter as Bangor won the Wonewoc-Center regional.

event: WIAA Division 4 sectional semifinal at La Crosse Central
recap: Blair-Taylor's quick guards, T.J. Nereng (22 points, eight assists) and Josh Peterson, ended Bangor's season at 22–2 in the WIAA Division 4 sectional semifinal, in front of an estimated 1,700 fans at La Crosse Central's Mark Sutton Gymnasium. The Wildcats led 34–28 at halftime. Bangor opened the second half on a 12–2 run, with 3-pointers from Lukas Ermis and Troy Bolcerek, who scored 26, but a 13–3 Blair-Taylor run gave the Wildcats a six-point lead after three quarters, and sophomore Jacob Stephenson scored 20 off Nereng's passes.

recap: Galesville won 10–5 at Bangor in the season finale, leaving Bangor 4–9. (The results page totals the opponents' points as 239, but its 13 scores add up to 244.)
Bangor opened the season by beating Melrose 22–10, the first of three games before the conference season.
Bangor beat Kendall 16–7 in its second game before the conference season.
Sparta beat Bangor 18–12, Bangor's only loss in its three games before the conference season.
Bangor opened the Coulee Conference season with an easy 21–4 win at Mindoro. (The season story dates it Dec. 5; the results list says Dec. 6.)
Holmen came to Bangor having usually beaten Bangor in the past, but Bangor won 25–16.
Onalaska beat Bangor 12–9 at Onalaska, Bangor's first conference loss.
A record crowd from both towns saw Bangor beat West Salem 26–10, its third win over West Salem in two years.
On a sub-zero night Bangor won 27–18 at Galesville, the defending conference champion, which had many veterans back.
Bangor beat Mindoro 26–5 to start the second round of conference games. Mindoro didn't score until about the last three minutes.
Holmen beat Bangor 22–13 at Holmen, helped by its long shots.
Bangor led from the start and beat Onalaska 25–13, avenging the December loss and keeping pace with Holmen for first place. (The season story dates it Feb. 6; the results list says Feb. 7.)
With much of Bangor along and a big West Salem crowd on hand, Bangor held on to beat West Salem 16–13. (The season story dates it Feb. 13; the results list says Feb. 14.)

Bangor beat Galesville 27–22 at home in its last conference game to keep the conference lead, its second win over Galesville that season. Bangor won the Coulee Conference title when Onalaska beat Holmen. (The season story dates it Feb. 20; the results list says Feb. 21.)
Bangor beat Aquinas 23–15 in a post-season game at La Crosse.

La Crosse Vocational beat Bangor 14–10 at Bangor in the last game before the tournament at Sparta (March 13–15), leaving Bangor 11–4. (The results page totals Bangor's points as 276, but its 15 scores add up to 298.)
Bangor beat La Crosse Aquinas 21–16 at Aquinas, a week after beating them 16–15 at Bangor. The book counts beating Aquinas twice among the season's highlights, along with winning the Coulee cup.

Camp Douglas beat Bangor 23–20 at the Sparta District Tournament, a day after Sparta beat Bangor 21–15, ending the season 11–5. The book calls it a good showing at Sparta, in Coach Harold Welch's first year at Bangor. Welch died in the summer of 1931, after his first year of teaching.

Tomah beat Bangor 31–11 in the final of the Sparta District Tournament, ending the season 13–5. Bangor had reached the final by winning the Sparta Elimination Tournament (Hillsboro and Kendall on March 5), then beating Mauston and Holmen. The book calls it probably one of the greatest teams in Bangor history, in Coach Rodney Martin's first year: second in the Coulee Conference and second at the district tournament.
Bangor beat West Salem 11–6 at Bangor, the first of two wins over West Salem that season, which the book names as one of the year's achievements.
Bangor beat West Salem 16–14 at West Salem, its second win over West Salem that season.
Bangor beat Camp Douglas, the Juneau County champions, 23–21 at Bangor.
Viola beat Bangor 22–18 in the Viroqua Supplementary Tournament, a day after Bangor beat Gays Mills 22–10, ending the season 10–8.
Bangor upset Galesville 20–17 at Bangor; the book says the loss practically ended Galesville's championship chances.

The YMCA beat Bangor 17–16 at Bangor, ending a 4–11 season. The book says the record was not as bad as it seems, with five of the 11 losses by one point (the scores listed show four one-point losses and a two-point loss at Holmen).
Bangor won 18–14 at Wilton for its fifth straight win to open the season, all against non-conference teams.
Bangor beat West Salem 19–16 at Bangor, ending a four-game losing streak (Mindoro, Holmen, Onalaska and Tomah).

Bangor opened the season by beating Viroqua, a Class A school, 22–16 at Bangor, although nearly everyone expected Bangor to lose. Viroqua led at halftime, but Bangor held them down in the second half.
The alumni scored four baskets in the first two minutes, on hook shots and more, led 13–11 at halftime and won 24–21.
Bangor beat Sparta, a Class A school, 12–11 at Bangor. The book says it was only the second time in Bangor's history that Bangor had beaten Sparta, in a game full of thrills.
Bangor beat Mindoro 26–17, making up for two losses to Mindoro the season before, with its best basketball of the season so far.
A slow game turned into a scoring spree. Bangor led only 7–5 at halftime, then scored 20 points in the second half while holding Onalaska to 6.
Back from a long Christmas break, Bangor took the lead early and never gave it up in a tense rivalry game at West Salem. A large group of Bangor students and town fans followed the team to the game.

Bangor beat Viroqua, the South Central Conference leaders, for the second time this season, 23–20 at Viroqua. Bangor led 11–3 at halftime, but Viroqua's fast breaks put them ahead 20–18 with two minutes left before Bangor scored the last five points.
Bangor beat Galesville 26–11 in a slow, loosely played game that the book calls a letdown, though it had its bright spots.
Bangor jumped out early, led 15–6 at halftime and won 35–15 in a rough game in Mindoro's small gym.
Holmen ended Bangor's seven-game winning streak, 18–16 at Holmen. It was Bangor's only conference loss of the season; the book says Bangor was well off its game against a powerful Holmen team.

Bangor beat Holmen in a conference game for the first time in four and a half seasons, keeping first place in the Coulee Conference. Bangor led 6–2 at halftime, and the second half was a back-and-forth battle of spectacular baskets.
After the 27–11 win in December this looked like an easy one, but Onalaska played hard. Bangor led 15–11 at halftime and had to hold on to win 26–23.
Before the biggest crowd of the season, Bangor beat West Salem 21–10, leading from the start and 7–3 at halftime.
On Sparta's large floor on a Tuesday night, Bangor scored the first seven points, but Sparta tied it 9–9 by halftime, scored the first two baskets of the second half and stayed ahead to win 18–14.

Bangor won its last conference game 37–14 at Galesville, its highest score of the season, with Reuben Filter scoring 17 points. Stopping at Holmen on the way home, the team learned that Onalaska had beaten Holmen 27–20, which broke the tie and gave Bangor its first Coulee Conference title in five years, and an invitation to the Reedsburg Class C tournament.

event: Class C district tournament at Reedsburg
recap: In the first round at Reedsburg, Bangor led Holmen 10–1 after one quarter and 16–8 at halftime. Holmen came back in the second half, and Bangor protected its three-point lead at the end by stalling. Wilfred Meier remembered scoring the game's first basket and first free throw.

event: Class C district tournament at Reedsburg
recap: Bangor led only 12–9 at halftime, then scored 20 points in the second half, 16 of them in the fourth quarter, to reach the final against Norwalk.

event: Class C district tournament at Reedsburg, final
recap: Bangor beat Norwalk 27–25 in overtime to become the first Bangor team to win a district tournament. Norwalk led 15–8 at halftime, and Bangor tied it 23–23 by the end of regulation. In overtime Bangor scored a basket and two free throws while Norwalk scored one basket. The book calls it the hardest-fought game of the tournament, and it was Bangor's first overtime game of the season.

At Boscobel, Bangor beat Barneveld, the Platteville district champions, 21–19 to win the region's place in the state tournament. Bangor held a small lead all game but was pressed throughout. Years later Jim Holmlund raised money for a 16-inch trophy for the school to mark the win.

event: Class C state tournament at Wisconsin Rapids
recap: In Bangor's first state tournament game, a late-morning game at the Lincoln Field House in Wisconsin Rapids, Fall Creek seemed to score from anywhere, led 27–3 at halftime and won 32–15.

event: Class C state tournament at Wisconsin Rapids, consolation
recap: In the consolation bracket, Bangor came from behind with a strong second half to beat Crivitz 29–21, a complete turnaround from the day before.

event: Class C state tournament at Wisconsin Rapids, consolation final
recap: Whitewater College High beat Bangor 21–16 on Friday afternoon for the consolation title. Bangor led most of the way and 10–8 at halftime, but three quick Whitewater baskets in the last few minutes decided it. Bangor finished fourth in the state Class C tournament, ending what the book calls the most successful season in Bangor's history.

Bangor opened its new gym with its third straight win over West Salem, which went on to reach the Division 3 sectional finals. A match-up zone held 6-8 Michael Southall to 10 points; Ryan Schroeder scored 16 and Justin Peterson 12, all on 3-pointers, and Bangor out-rebounded the Panthers 29-27. Peterson's 12 points were all on 3-pointers, and David Sackmaster led West Salem with 19. "I don't know that we have a home court advantage yet, but it was nice to get off on the right foot," coach Don Addington told the Tribune.

In the conference opener Bangor led 23-16 at halftime and by 17 late in the third quarter, but Necedah answered with a 22-4 run to take a one-point lead with 2:00 left. Shane Amundson tied it from the line, and after Necedah missed a final shot, Scott Greeno was fouled with five seconds left and made the second free throw for the win.

Royall, the conference favorite, controlled the game from the opening tip. The Panthers shot 56% to Bangor's 23%, made 64% of their free throws to Bangor's 33% and out-rebounded the Cardinals 37-28, and Bangor turned the ball over 23 times. Josh Board scored 27 for Royall, 14 of them in the first quarter.

Bangor beat state-ranked Hillsboro in double overtime. The Tigers took the lead in the fourth quarter, but Sam Williams scored with 30 seconds left to tie it at 42, and Greg Johnson tied it again at 48 with 15 seconds left in the first overtime. Bangor opened the second overtime with an 8-0 run. Bangor made 8 of 14 free throws in the second overtime. The teams combined for 57 turnovers; Ben Campbell led Bangor with 16 points and 8 rebounds.

event: Warrior Club Holiday Classic at Winona State, first round
recap: In the opening round of the Warrior Club Holiday Classic at Winona State, Bangor shot 46% from the field and 63% from the line, its first game over 50% at the line. Justin Peterson scored 15, Shane Amundson 13 and Ben Campbell 11.

event: Warrior Club Holiday Classic at Winona State, championship
recap: Bangor won the Warrior Club Holiday Classic over Blair-Taylor, ranked first in Division 4 before the season. The Cardinals scored the game's first 12 points without a miss, trailed 30-27 at halftime and by eight with four minutes left, then held the Wildcats to one point the rest of regulation. Ben Campbell's two free throws with seven seconds left were answered by a Blair-Taylor free throw, and Bangor made 9 free throws in overtime. Shane Amundson scored 20 and made the all-tournament team. The wins over West Salem, Hillsboro and Blair-Taylor moved Bangor to seventh in the state's Division 4 rankings.

Bangor trailed by two after the first quarter, then outscored Brookwood 42-20 over the next two to lead by 20. The Falcons scored 22 in the fourth, but Bangor held on at the free throw line to go 3-1 in the conference and 6-1 overall.

Against a highly rated Melrose-Mindoro team, also 6-1, Bangor led 10-6 after a quarter. Nate Hamilton hit three 3-pointers in the third to keep it close, and Sam Williams tied it at 49 with 1:20 left, but the Mustangs retook the lead at the free throw line. Bangor was fouled on a rebound with one second left and missed the front end. Despite the loss Bangor moved up to sixth in the state rankings.
Cashton tied the game at 23 by halftime behind 12 second-quarter points from Fronk, but Bangor used its Iowa baseline offense against the Eagles' 3-2 zone to win. Justin Peterson scored 20.

Bangor outscored defending conference champion New Lisbon in each of the first three quarters to lead by 24, and everyone scored. Justin Franke and Nate Hamilton had 13 points each. Bangor was 5-1 in the conference and 8-2 overall, a game behind Royall.

The first of four straight road losses. Bangor led at halftime behind 13 points from Justin Peterson and two Ryan Schroeder 3-pointers, but Necedah opened the third quarter with a 15-6 run. Schroeder's 3 tied it with 33 seconds left before Ebert's bank shot won it for Necedah, and Bangor's 3-pointer at the buzzer fell short.
In a low-scoring game against Gale-Ettrick-Trempealeau's zone, Bangor trailed by 11 going into the fourth quarter and got to the free throw line 20 times in the quarter but made only 8.

Bangor led Royall 17-16 midway through the second quarter, then went 1 for 10 from the field as the Panthers built a nine-point halftime lead. Royall's six 3-pointers and 15 free throws to Bangor's four were the difference.

Bangor led by one at halftime at Hillsboro, and Ryan Schroeder answered Bruha's nine third-quarter points with 11 of his own, including three 3-pointers, but Bangor made only 2 of 9 shots in the fourth quarter.

Bangor ended a four-game losing streak against Wonewoc-Center, in a game first scheduled earlier in the season and snowed out. Bangor held Benish and Gehri to four points in the first half and led by 12 early in the third quarter; Nate Hamilton's 3-pointer made it 64-59 with two minutes left, and Bangor made 7 free throws in the last minute.

Justin Peterson scored 17 of his season-high 25 points in the first half as Bangor led Brookwood 44-26, and he had the first Bangor dunks since 1990 (only the second one counted). Bangor led by 27 with 5:40 left before Mullenberg made five shots in a row, three of them 3-pointers, to cut it to seven.
On the 10th annual Alumni Weekend, Bangor trailed Seneca 4-3 in the first quarter, took the lead on a Justin Franke basket and led the rest of the way. Nate Hamilton led with 11.

Cashton led 23-22 after three quarters before Justin Peterson took over, scoring 19 of Bangor's 27 fourth-quarter points on 5 of 5 shooting and 7 of 7 free throws, with two 3-pointers and a dunk. He finished with 22.

In the make-up game at Wonewoc-Center, the Indians scored the last seven points of the first half to lead by four and ended the third quarter on an 11-2 run for a 54-40 lead. Bangor shot 3 for 15 in the fourth quarter; Benish and Gehri combined for 44 points.
Bangor finished the regular season 9-5 in the conference and 13-7 overall, shooting 24 of 47 from the field and 17 of 23 at the line while holding New Lisbon to 17 field goals.

In the regional at Greenwood, Bangor trailed 13-7 after a quarter, then outscored Greenwood 12-4 in the second for a 19-17 halftime lead. Greenwood led 32-31 with 4:40 left; Justin Peterson made four free throws to tie it at 39 with a minute left, Bangor missed a breakaway layup, and Greenwood's big man scored and was fouled with 25 seconds left for the win. Blair-Taylor, which Bangor would have played next, went on to the state tournament.

Joel Ziehme scored with one second left, on a pass from Kyle Swogger after a steal, to give Luther a 49–47 win in the season opener. Brad Skaer, a former Luther student, scored 32 points with four 3-pointers and 10 rebounds, but fouled out just after his last 3 put Bangor ahead 47–44, and Bangor didn't score again.

Brad Skaer scored 40 points, going 6 for 8 from 3-point range and 12 for 13 at the free-throw line, as Bangor opened the Scenic Bluffs season with a win. (Wonewoc-Center's quarter scores after the first can't be read in the clipping.)

Brad Skaer scored 36 points with three 3-pointers, giving him 32, 40 and 36 in Bangor's first three games, and Chris Chandler had 11 points and 11 rebounds as Bangor led the whole game. (The paper's quarter scores for Bangor add to 62, one less than its final, so its third and fourth quarters are left blank.)

New Lisbon held Brad Skaer, who came in averaging 36 points a game, to six points through three quarters while building a 47–33 lead. Skaer scored 17 in the fourth for a team-high 23, but it was too late. Troy Bolcerek scored 12 in his first game of the season after spraining his ankle, and New Lisbon's David Paradise led all scorers with 26.

Auburndale, coached by 1963 Bangor graduate Tim Anderson, scored the first five points and never trailed. The Apaches led 28–23 at halftime, then opened the second half on a 19–8 run, with Dan Weinfurter scoring eight of his 16 in the third quarter. Auburndale held the ball for nearly three minutes on one fourth-quarter possession and kept Bangor scoreless over the final 58 seconds. Brad Skaer, averaging about 30 points, was held to 17, nine of them in the fourth, and Troy Bolcerek added 16.

Bangor handed Cashton its first Scenic Bluffs loss, holding the Eagles without a field goal in the second quarter, which Bangor won 13–5. Cashton's only points that quarter came at the free-throw line, where it went 11 for 21 for the game. Brad Skaer led Bangor with 12 points and 8 rebounds, Kyle Schroeder added 11, and Troy Bolcerek had 6 points and 4 assists.

A meeting of former coaching colleagues: first-year West Salem coach Don Addington led Bangor's program from 1984 to 1998 with Joe Stekel as his top assistant, and he still taught at Bangor High School. Dustin Wehrs scored 24 and Addington's son Ben 16, going 6 for 6 at the line, as West Salem made 16 of 22 free throws. Brad Skaer scored 30 points with 11 rebounds, his fourth 30-point game of the season, and Troy Bolcerek's desperation shot at the end hit the backboard and rimmed out.
Royall broke open a battle of second-place Scenic Bluffs teams with a 23-point third quarter. Sam Overlien led Royall with 19, and Brad Skaer had a game-high 21 for Bangor.

Brad Skaer scored 17 of his game-high 29 points in the second quarter as Bangor took control of the nonconference game, and Troy Bolcerek scored all 10 of his in the third. Josh House led Melrose-Mindoro with 10.
Bangor led by 12 through three quarters and held on at Ontario. Kyle Schroeder led the Cardinals with 11 points and Troy Bolcerek added 10; Jon Wopat had 13 for Brookwood.
Brad Skaer scored a game-high 25 and Chris Chandler added 14 points and 8 rebounds as Bangor moved into a three-way tie for second place in the Scenic Bluffs.
Troy Bolcerek scored 18 points and Bangor took a 16-4 first-quarter lead on the way to its fourth straight win. Jeff Raese led Wonewoc-Center with 12.
Brad Skaer hit five 3-pointers and scored 22 points in the nonconference win, and Troy Bolcerek and Chris Chandler added 12 apiece. Matt Deck led Arcadia with 13.

Bangor led by 11 at halftime, then outscored Hillsboro 22-9 in the third quarter. Brad Skaer, the area's leading scorer at 22.5 points a game, led the way; the Tribune gave him 15 points and the Coulee News 18. Paul Langrehr, Chris Chandler and Brandon Meyer each had seven rebounds, and Nick Hora led Hillsboro with 16. "There was great overall team effort on offense and defense," coach Joe Stekel said.

After seven straight wins, Bangor beat New Lisbon to move into a first-place tie with the Rockets in the Scenic Bluffs. Brad Skaer had 26 points, 20 of them in the first half, and Bangor held New Lisbon to 5-for-19 shooting in the first quarter. The Tribune gave Skaer seven rebounds and the Coulee News five. Mark Willer led New Lisbon with 22. "I felt we came out with a lot of intensity and focus," coach Joe Stekel said. "We had outstanding play at both ends of the court."

Bangor kept pace with New Lisbon atop the Scenic Bluffs, jumping out 14-4 in the first quarter before Cashton outscored the Cardinals 25-17 in the fourth. The middle quarters aren't known. Brad Skaer scored 17 and Kyle Schroeder 15, and Troy Bolcerek had seven rebounds. "This was a game where we did what we had to do to win the game," coach Joe Stekel said.

Brad Skaer grabbed the rebound of Sam Hanson's missed turnaround with four seconds left, dribbled up the sideline and hit a 15-foot pull-up jumper at the buzzer for Bangor's ninth straight win, in front of 1,100 fans at the Bangor gym. Royall had gone on an 18-10 run in the third quarter for a 35-34 lead. Skaer shot 5 for 21 but the win gave Bangor control of the conference; Troy Bolcerek led with 17 points, 13 in the first half. "Brad is as good a kid as we have to take that shot," coach Joe Stekel said. The Coulee News gave Chris Chandler nine rebounds and Skaer eight; the Tribune box score has Chandler with seven. The box score printed Bangor's line-score total as 53 and Zach Thayer with 6 points, both misprints.

Bangor clinched a share of the Scenic Bluffs title, its first since 1987, leading 35-14 at halftime after holding Brookwood to two points in the second quarter. Brad Skaer had 16 points and eight rebounds, leaving him 11 points short of 1,000 for his career, and Chris Chandler added 11 and Troy Bolcerek 10. "We had great team defense, holding Brookwood to 34 points," coach Joe Stekel said. "It feels good to be the conference champions," Skaer said.

Aaron Salsman scored 13 of his 28 points in the second quarter as Gale-Ettrick-Trempealeau built a 56-25 halftime lead in the nonconference game. Brad Skaer scored 10 of his 20 points in the second quarter and hit three 3-pointers.

Bangor won the Scenic Bluffs title outright for the first time since 1987. Necedah led 11-9 after one quarter and 22-20 at halftime, but a 10-5 Bangor run in the third quarter put the Cardinals ahead for good; the last two quarters aren't known. Brad Skaer scored 24 of Bangor's 48 points. "I am happy for the boys basketball program because they achieved the goal which they had set earlier in the season," coach Joe Stekel said.

Brad Skaer scored 33 points, 27 in the first half, going 14 for 19 from the field and 5 for 9 from 3-point range. Bangor led 46-4 at halftime, and La Farge didn't score its first basket until 3:17 was left in the half. Matt Benson led La Farge (0-21) with 13.

Top-seeded Bangor jumped out to a 16-0 lead, seven of the points by Troy Bolcerek, who finished with a game-high 14, then "survived" the rest of the way, as coach Joe Stekel put it. Brad Skaer was held to 11 points and missed four of five free throws, but the bench helped: Paul Langrehr's 3-pointer and runner stretched the lead to 22 early in the third quarter. Bangor held Weston scoreless for five minutes in the second quarter and four in the third. "I guess it's good to win the ugly ones," Skaer said.

event: WIAA Division 4 regional final at Cashton
recap: After a sleepy first half, Bangor's pressure defense sparked an 11-0 run to open the second half for a 38-18 lead, and the Cardinals won their second regional title in three years. Troy Bolcerek led all scorers with 21 points and 12 rebounds and was 3 for 3 from 3-point range in the first quarter; Brad Skaer added 16 by the story's count. Wonewoc-Center's Jeff Raese picked up his fourth foul 33 seconds into the third quarter and later fouled out, and Todd Gehri led the Indians with 16. "We let them hang around in the first half, but we came out in the second half and put them away," Bolcerek said. In the box score, Skaer's line (4-13, one 3-pointer, 6-6) adds up to 15 points and Brandon Meyer's to 0, not the 16 and 2 printed, and Dereck Kamwesa's to 0, not 2; the corrected lines match both team totals.

event: WIAA Division 4 sectional semifinal at Logan
recap: In front of 2,000 fans at La Crosse Logan, Bangor opened with an 11-0 run for a 13-2 lead, and Brad Skaer's steal and layup put the Cardinals up 50-48 with 3:42 left. Greenwood answered with inside baskets by 6-foot-7 Josh Gopsar (18 points, 15 rebounds), and after Kyle Schroeder's 3-pointer cut it to 54-53 and Troy Bolcerek's jumper to 56-55 with 58 seconds left, a Steve Krause layup and two Matt McFarlane free throws ended Bangor's season at 17-7. Skaer had 30 points and seven rebounds; Nathan Langrehr played through a hurt knee until fouling out in the fourth quarter. "I'm so proud of this team. I've had three great years here," Skaer said. "I am very proud of what we have accomplished this year, winning conference and regionals," coach Joe Stekel said.
